subject: im
question: EOQ numericals: formula EOQ = sqrt(2DS/H), a worked example and how to solve the class sums.
title: EOQ Sums, Fully Solved
hook: Nine thousand units, one formula, one answer.
answer: EOQ = square root of (2DS / H); D = yearly demand, S = cost of placing one order, H = holding cost per unit per year.
Example: D = 9,000, S = Rs 200, H = Rs 10. EOQ = sqrt(2 x 9,000 x 200 / 10) = sqrt(360,000) = 600 units.
Ordering cost = 15 x 200 = Rs 3,000; holding cost = (600 / 2) x 10 = Rs 3,000; total cost = Rs 6,000 (ordering = holding at the EOQ).
Method: write D, S, H in yearly units (if H is a percentage, H = % x unit price); apply the formula; orders = D / EOQ; total cost = ordering + holding.
